source.title: Learning through atypical "phase transitions" in overparameterized neural networks
source.authors: Carlo Baldassi; Clarissa Lauditi; E. M. Malatesta; R. Pacelli; Gabriele Perugini; R. Zecchina

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own test/generalization-error results across model sizes and argues that these settings show monotonically decreasing error rather than a double-descent curve.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses and cites prior double-descent results, which are not recorded as findings here. Rows below are for the paper's own error-versus-overparameterization results. It does not report test error over epochs or an increase in error from increasing training-set size near interpolation.
record.test_reason: The paper's own error-versus-size sweeps bear on whether test error peaks near interpolation. These include analytic binary random-features curves, a tree committee machine, an MLP and a CIFAR10 CNN, all noiseless teacher or clean-label settings. It never explicitly argues that double descent is wrong; it mentions double descent only in related work. So this is T3 (new setting with a result), not T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors' central claim is about atypical, wide, solution-dense regions that appear at a Local Entropy transition beyond the interpolation threshold, and about learning algorithms finding them. Improving generalization with overparameterization is reported as an observation; the authors do not present it as a refutation of double descent.
record.recipe_differences: The study combines statistical-physics analysis of a binary random-features model with numerical checks on committee machines, a multilayer perceptron, and a CNN. It does not reproduce the original double-descent size/epoch/sample sweeps or their measurement recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports different generalization-error plateaus and algorithmic thresholds for different optimization schemes and initializations. In the CNN, training-set fit begins at C = 50 for SGD and C = 60 for ADAM.

fits_no_version.finding: Efficient algorithms cannot fit data between the information-theoretic interpolation threshold α_c and the Local Entropy threshold α_LE. In practice, the 'interpolation point' reached by algorithms lies beyond α_c.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In non-convex networks, the size at which training algorithms begin to interpolate exceeds the information-theoretic interpolation threshold. This would shift where any double-descent peak occurs.

record.problems: Several relevant error-versus-size results are only plotted, without numerical values in the text. The numerical experiments use specific synthetic tasks or datasets and settings; the paper itself calls for further studies on larger deep networks.
record.rows_left_out: No additional error-versus-size results were left out. Test-error-versus-alpha_T plots vary a teacher/data ratio in the large-overparameterization regime, not training sample count near the interpolation threshold, and therefore were not cataloged for V3. Training-error and local-energy plots were not recorded as test-error results.

untested.parts: Whether a peak appears with label noise; only clean-label CIFAR10 and parity-MNIST are used. The MLP curve shape is not stated.
The underparameterized side and peak are not computed for the analytic binary random-features model. Kernel and other non-network model classes are not tested.
Not tested; there are no test-error-over-epochs curves.
Not tested. The α_T sweeps sit in the large-overparameterization regime, not near interpolation.
Not tested; label noise and regularization are not varied.

missing.what: Numerical fBP and BP-barycenter generalization error versus 1/α. In the large-overparameterization regime, fBP tracks the zero-margin barycenter curve.
missing.locator: Fig. 2 left panel (blue and yellow points)

missing.what: Train and test error versus 1/α for MCT0, SBPI and BP on the binary perceptron at α_T=5

record.verdict_notes: The settings are noiseless (teacher-generated labels, clean CIFAR10). Original double-descent work finds the peak strongest with label noise, so the V1 and V4 challenges may reflect noise dependence (V6) rather than a general absence. The analytic curves cannot show a peak, because error is only defined for interpolating solutions.

versions.untested_parts: The reported deep-network size sweeps do not establish behavior outside the tested size ranges or test whether the peak is located near the size that just fits the training set.
The study does not test every model class, nor does it establish a universal curve across model classes.

rows.subject: binary non-convex random features model, typical solutions
rows.operation_detail: Analytically varied degree of overparameterization and computed generalization error.
rows.measure: Generalization error versus degree of overparameterization 1/alpha
rows.note: The text states that all plotted generalization-error curves are monotonically decreasing; this is the zero-margin typical-solution curve.
rows.check: Typical-solution error is defined only where zero-error solutions exist (1/α > 1/α_c). The curve covers only the post-interpolation side, so no peak can appear. A monotone decrease from α_c means error is highest at the threshold, which matches V4's second descent. 'Absent' is wrong.
